inspiration: One sprite set, many looks: a single 8-bit index texture is recoloured by swapping a 256-entry palette in the fragment shader (data/shaders/applypalette.frag, line 12). Recreate a per-zone tint or a damage flash this way with our own palettes.

Named palette sets as separate files (base, map_base, map_glass, map_translucent, marker, and a darken step in resources/palettes/base) make it easy to give the map, the HUD and the world each their own ramp.
Glyph sheets in three size tiers (bold, small, tiny) per character (resources/fonts/latin) keep text readable at several sizes. For a 375 px phone HUD the same idea gives one font with a size ladder.
A translucent map palette (resources/palettes/map_glass) suggests a dimmed glass overlay for a minimap or world map where the terrain stays readable underneath.
Scenario changes are shipped as small data-only patch files (data/scenario_patches, 142 files) rather than code. Content tweaks can ship as data without a release of the engine.
Locale strings use stable ids (STR_XXXX) and inline value tokens ({COMMA16}, {STRINGID}) so the same sentence can carry numbers in any language (data/language/en-GB.txt line 2 describes the format).

briefs.label: Glass map overlay
briefs.why: A translucent tinted layer over the terrain keeps the map readable and reads as a separate view layer, which suits a 375 px map sheet.
briefs.keep: a translucent overlay palette separate from the base palette; the terrain stays visible under the overlay
briefs.change: our overlay uses a cool steel ramp and a grid-free look; no dark glass border; overlay opacity set per zone
briefs.ref: resources/palettes/map_glass/ and resources/palettes/map_translucent/ (not read beyond folder names)

briefs.label: Per-zone palette swap
briefs.why: One art set recoloured per zone gives a fast biome change without new art files.
briefs.keep: a single index texture with a 256-entry palette lookup in the fragment stage
briefs.change: our swap is a zone colour grade (lighting tint), not ride or team colours; the palette is zone data, not a file per variant

briefs.label: Three-size glyph ladder
briefs.why: Pre-drawn small and tiny glyphs stay sharp at small sizes where scaling a large glyph would blur.
briefs.keep: one glyph set in several pixel sizes for the same face
briefs.change: our HUD uses one sans family with weight steps for 375 px phones, not a pixel font
